sections.crash_profile: From {{window_start}} to {{window_end}}, {{total_3y}} crashes occurred at this unsignalized intersection, with {{ka_3y}} fatal or serious injury (K or A) and {{kabc_3y}} KABCO injury crashes. The most frequent types were angle ({{angle_3y}}), rear-end ({{rear_end_3y}}), and left-turn opposing ({{left_turn_opposing_3y}}). Night and wet conditions contributed to {{night_3y}} and {{wet_3y}} crashes respectively. Pedestrian and bicycle counts are not available.
sections.why_flagged: Flagged due to the model estimate of {{fsi_rate}} fatal or serious injury crashes per mile per year, elevated traffic exposure ({{aadt}} vehicles/day), proximity to schools, and a high density of crashes and injury crashes within 250 meters. The intersection is on a state route and included in the High Injury Network.

countermeasures.rationale: This systemic signing and marking improvement package is supported by broader evidence for all crash types and KABCO severities, per CMF {{cmf:8867}}. The entry is not a direct match for fatal or serious injury crashes and requires engineering review to confirm applicability and prerequisites.

Flashing beacons at stop-controlled intersections have broader evidence for all crash types and severities, per CMF {{cmf:446}}. This entry is not a direct match for fatal or serious injury crashes and needs engineering review to verify prerequisites and installation details.

sections.benefit_cost: A benefit could not be computed for either countermeasure, as no audit-approved CMF, unit cost, or service life is available, and the severity scope does not match fatal or serious injury crashes.
sections.next_steps: Conduct engineering review to verify intersection geometry, traffic volumes, and existing equipment for both treatments. Confirm that prerequisites for systemic signing/marking improvements and flashing beacons are met. Assess site-specific suitability and coordinate with TxDOT due to jurisdiction.
